likely_fatal_first.claim: The mean-zero pairwise quotient target is the load-bearing object that makes correction candidate-specific and transports e_t.
likely_fatal_first.why_selected: Every r_ij is formed from the same K scalar residuals u_k = Y_k - s_k^0, so a direct set scorer may recover exactly the same centered corrections without any pairwise quotient; moreover the loss contains no term that forces its output to depend on e_t rather than candidate features.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 1. Instantiate existing LIBERO and RoboTwin2.0 tasks with open-weight π0.5 and a DreamZero-compatible open-weight WAM; log RGB, proprioception, language, executed chunks, WAM predictions, and terminal success, producing factual-transition records.
produces: factual-transition records containing h_t, b_{t-1}, predicted/real observations, and success labels
formalized_procedure.note: Well-typed; environment state is available only for training/evaluation rollback.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 2. Train g_φ on frozen WAM future latents and benchmark language to predict terminal success probability; its inputs are predicted candidate trajectories and its output is s_k^0 in success-probability units.
formalized_procedure.note: The probability interpretation is valid for s_k^0, but not automatically for s_k^0+c_k because c_k is identified only modulo a common offset.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 3. For each training record, execute b_{t-1}, snapshot the exact post-prefix simulator state, compute e_t from the real and previously predicted current observations, sample K current π0.5 candidates, and output one matched branch bundle.
formalized_procedure.note: The executed residual and branch snapshot refer to the same post-prefix transition. σ_p has no zero-variance guard; changing its value changes e_t, but its estimation rule is bound. K is named, defaults to 8, and is selected from {4,8,16}.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 4. Restore the snapshot for every candidate, execute that candidate and then the standard π0.5 continuation, and output Y_k plus all r_{ij}; these rollback outcomes are training and evaluation labels only.
formalized_procedure.note: The branch label and declared future-success estimand match at the same post-prefix state; each Y_k is a noisy realization of the conditional outcome, not the conditional expectation itself.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 5. Train the permutation-equivariant quotient head on each full bundle, subtract its mean correction across candidates, and optimize pairwise center and interval losses; inputs are h_t, e_t, candidate actions, and WAM futures, and outputs are c_k and w_{ij}.
formalized_procedure.note: Center differences are antisymmetric and cycle-consistent. However r_ij is algebraically equivalent to direct centered u_k supervision, and neither the loss nor architecture forces dependence on e_t. Width symmetry w_ij=w_ji is not stated.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 6. On held-out episodes, compute q_α from the maximum pair nonconformity per candidate bundle and choose α on the coverage-abstention frontier, producing one set-calibrated interval rule.
formalized_procedure.note: Operative terms admit two readings: coverage of realized Y_i-Y_j versus coverage of the conditional mean ρ_ij. Only realized-outcome predictive coverage follows from split conformal. The nonconformity formula, finite-sample quantile, width symmetry, and separation of α/K selection from calibration are undefined, so the coverage claim is conditional until patched.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 7. At deployment after each real prefix, generate K new executable candidate chunks, run the WAM and g_φ, compute e_t, and run one quotient-head forward pass to produce s_k and D_{ij}; no rollback or hidden simulator state enters this path.
formalized_procedure.note: No simulator artifact is consumed. D_ij uses un-clipped contrasts while s_k is clipped, so the two disagree whenever clipping activates; s_k is not a calibrated marginal probability because the common offset is discarded.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 8. Compute M_t and either execute the robust winner or invoke the L_safe fallback; this comparison changes which current π0.5 chunk reaches the robot, and the next real observation closes the receding-horizon loop.
produces: executed robust winner or fallback action
formalized_procedure.note: Defined for K>=2. K=0 or K=1 makes max/min reductions invalid; exact M_t=0 correctly falls back, but tie-breaking of the uncorrected top candidate is unspecified.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 9. Evaluate uncorrected WAM ranking, shared-gain residual injection, independent marginal residual regression, FBFM, and Residual Quotient on identical snapshots; output latent error, pairwise inversion rate, Kendall rank correlation, top-1 regret, task success, abstention rate, and inference latency.
produces: prediction, ranking, success, abstention, and latency metrics
formalized_procedure.note: Evaluation is matched; it does not repair the training objective's inability to identify e_t usage.

formalized_procedure.verbatim_quote: 10. Run the e_t permutation, branch-label shuffling, width ablation, and full rollback-oracle controls; each intervention propagates through D_{ij} and M_t to the selected physical action and final task success.
formalized_procedure.note: These are empirical diagnostics. They can reveal bypass after training but do not structurally prevent the quotient head from ignoring e_t.

final_candidate.title: Residual Quotient: Pairwise-Identified Correction for Current Action Suffixes
final_candidate.hook: A factual WAM residual can reduce next-frame latent error yet increase rollback top-1 action regret when candidate suffixes induce different contact mechanisms. Residual Quotient predicts only sign-stable pairwise outcome corrections and abstains when the realized transition does not identify a current winner.
final_candidate.hook_shape_rationale: Shape (a), surprising empirical reveal, is admitted by the predicted opposite directions of latent prediction error and rollback top-1 regret on the same current-state candidate sets. Shape (c) was viable because the frozen VLA and WAM gain only a small correction head, but it was rejected because parameter minimalism is not the load-bearing claim.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier leaf establishes when the residual observed after one action retains its direction and scale for a different candidate action, versus when the candidate lies outside action support or invokes a different contact mechanism and must not inherit that residual; this is the unresolved residue of execution-time re-grounding in semanticscholar:a77ce57cc8614da8e469228797af4c69274a1428 and trust-based execution in dblp:journals/corr/abs-2605-06222. — stakes: manipulation users can receive confidently worsened actions after perturbations, while the field lacks conditions under which online WAM correction is causally interpretable rather than accidental.
gap_closure.how_closed: Corpus support is thin in robot WAMs: C01 relocates correction from a marginal pixel/latent residual to the quotient of pairwise current-suffix outcome residuals, while heterogeneous_decomposition uses its calibrated sign interval to separate candidate pairs into correctable and abstained regimes.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier leaf evaluates whether corrected futures improve the true ordering of multiple VLA action candidates under rollback-simulator outcomes, rather than merely reducing visual or latent prediction discrepancy; this remains open after the prediction-space corrections of semanticscholar:a77ce57cc8614da8e469228797af4c69274a1428 and the training-time fidelity constraints of arxiv:2608.13489. — stakes: practitioners can spend WAM compute selecting a worse action despite prettier predictions, and intellectually the link from world-model accuracy to decision quality remains unvalidated.
gap_closure.how_closed: Corpus support is thin in robot WAMs: C02 supplies same-snapshot rollback candidate bundles whose independent simulator outcomes isolate decision-order fidelity from the confound of lower pixel or latent reconstruction error.

final_candidate.core_mechanism: At decision time t, after the robot has executed the previous action chunk b_{t-1}, the method fixes the real current history h_t of RGB, proprioception, and executed actions and samples K = 8 current executable suffix chunks from the open-weight π0.5 policy; K is swept over {4, 8, 16} and chosen by held-out success per inference latency. With an open-weight DreamZero-compatible WAM, it forms the factual residual e_t = [E(o_t) - E(ô_t^-); (p_t - p̂_t^-)/σ_p], where ô_t^- and p̂_t^- are the WAM predictions made before b_{t-1}, E is fixed to the last spatial encoder block before temporal dynamics, σ_p is the training-set per-coordinate proprioceptive standard deviation, and brackets denote concatenation rather than addition across units. For each current candidate a_t^k, the frozen WAM produces a future latent trajectory Ẑ_k and a learned outcome head g_φ(Ẑ_k, language) produces the baseline simulator-success probability s_k^0; g_φ is trained only from existing LIBERO and RoboTwin2.0 terminal success labels. During training only, an exact simulator snapshot taken after b_{t-1} is restored for all K candidates, each candidate is executed and then followed by π0.5 closed-loop continuation, and its oracle outcome Y_k is recorded, yielding the pairwise residual target r_{ij} = (Y_i - Y_j) - (s_i^0 - s_j^0). A permutation-equivariant Set Transformer consumes h_t, e_t, and the whole candidate set and outputs mean-zero candidate corrections c_k plus nonnegative pair widths w_{ij}; it is trained on r_{ij} through differences c_i - c_j, so antisymmetry and cycle consistency hold by construction while the unidentified common residual offset is explicitly discarded. Split conformal calibration on held-out mechanism and contact perturbations adds the episode-wise maximum nonconformity q_α to every pair width, with α = 0.10 selected from {0.05, 0.10, 0.20} by the validation coverage-abstention frontier; the resulting interval D_{ij} = [s_i^0 - s_j^0 + c_i - c_j - w_{ij} - q_α, s_i^0 - s_j^0 + c_i - c_j + w_{ij} + q_α] has empirical simultaneous coverage under exchangeable calibration episodes from the stated simulator and π0.5 candidate process. The corrected candidate probability is s_k = clip(s_k^0 + c_k, 0, 1), and the load-bearing transport margin is M_t = max_i min_{j≠i} inf D_{ij}: when M_t > 0 the corresponding current candidate is executed, while otherwise the method abstains, executes L_safe = 1 controller interval from the uncorrected π0.5 top candidate, and immediately replans; L_safe is fixed to the minimum executable controller interval. The shared evaluation reports rollback pairwise inversion rate and top-1 regret from those same post-prefix snapshots alongside latent prediction error, so a prettier but decision-worse correction is visible. No simulator oracle is used at deployment: the just-observed factual residual affects newly generated current suffixes through the learned quotient head, and no obsolete action, recursive branch carrier, shared-noise twin rollout, or hidden-parameter posterior is executed or inferred online. Calibration uses disjoint model-training, hyperparameter-selection, and calibration episodes: after K and alpha are fixed on the selection split, enforce w_ij=w_ji, define each calibration-bundle score R_b=max_{i<j} max(0, |r_ij-(c_i-c_j)|-w_ij), and set q_alpha to the ceil((n_cal+1)(1-alpha))-th ordered R_b (q_alpha=+infinity when that rank exceeds n_cal); D_ij then targets simultaneous predictive coverage of the realized pair outcomes Y_i-Y_j for a fresh exchangeable bundle from the same fixed candidate process, not coverage of the conditional mean estimand. Because the pairwise supervision discards the common residual offset, s_k=clip(s_k^0+c_k,0,1) is only a bounded display score and is not claimed to be a calibrated marginal success probability; all selection and coverage statements use the un-clipped pairwise contrast centers in D_ij.
final_candidate.core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 — PREMISES LEDGER
P1: A contact or dynamics mismatch revealed by the just-executed prefix persists into at least some immediate current suffixes but can change with candidate-induced contact mode — untested — falsification target; without partial persistence e_t cannot improve current ranking, while universal persistence would make abstention unnecessary.
P2 observation-model: training branch outcomes are observed by restoring the exact post-prefix LIBERO or RoboTwin2.0 simulator state and drawing all candidate chunks from the same π0.5 sampler used at evaluation; this makes candidate comparisons conditionally matched inside the scripted perturbation family, but exchangeability can fail under unseen real physics.
P3: RGB plus proprioceptive residuals contain some information about hidden contact mismatch even without tactile sensing — untested — falsification target; visible pose and motion error often reflect contact, but the negative-control permutation directly tests whether that information is useful.
P4: terminal simulator success after a candidate chunk plus π0.5 continuation is the relevant decision outcome; this is believed because it measures the downstream task rather than WAM reconstruction, but claims are scoped to LIBERO and RoboTwin2.0 tasks and the π0.5 proposal distribution.
ESTIMAND: for each ordered pair in a current candidate bundle, ρ_{ij}(h_t,e_t,A_t) = E[(Y_i-Y_j) - (s_i^0-s_j^0) | h_t,e_t,A_t] over the simulator perturbation, continuation, and π0.5 candidate process, represented only modulo an action-independent common offset, together with an empirical simultaneous prediction interval over all pairs in the bundle.
BLOCK 2 — NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT
The runnable naive baseline projects e_t into every candidate WAM future with one shared gain and chooses the candidate with the largest corrected success probability. Branch (i): it silently assumes the factual residual has candidate-invariant direction and scale, which is false when suffixes create different contact modes; the proposed K-way branch target learns pairwise residual differences and refuses comparisons whose calibrated interval crosses zero, directly confronting that failure. Standard-tool follow-up: conformal prediction is textbook, but this instance requires simultaneous coverage over a dynamically generated action set whose labels share one post-prefix physical state and disappear at deployment; the contribution is the mean-zero pairwise quotient target plus episode-maximum set calibration that changes the executed action, not conformal calibration alone.
BLOCK 3 — DESIGN RATIONALE
The transport and ranking gaps share the same post-prefix rollback candidate bundle, and removing ranking evaluation would make the correction claim unverifiable, whereas the deferred representation-necessity diagnostic would require a separate intervention family. Marginal residual regression was rejected as the occupied learned-residual node, latent-parameter abduction as classical Bayes-adaptive system identification or CF-GPS-like inference, and shared-noise twin/JMDP rollouts as requiring a counterfactual coupling online; here K-way branches are supervision only and deployment predicts a set-valued quotient. Same-carrier recursive re-anchoring, functional-gradient boundary scores, geometry-action crossovers, censoring replay, and fixed-scaffold regret were also rejected because they recreate the named soft-negative mechanism families rather than the current-suffix pairwise estimand.
final_candidate.core_mechanism_steps:
1. Instantiate existing LIBERO and RoboTwin2.0 tasks with open-weight π0.5 and a DreamZero-compatible open-weight WAM; log RGB, proprioception, language, executed chunks, WAM predictions, and terminal success, producing factual-transition records.
2. Train g_φ on frozen WAM future latents and benchmark language to predict terminal success probability; its inputs are predicted candidate trajectories and its output is s_k^0 in success-probability units.
3. For each training record, execute b_{t-1}, snapshot the exact post-prefix simulator state, compute e_t from the real and previously predicted current observations, sample K current π0.5 candidates, and output one matched branch bundle.
4. Restore the snapshot for every candidate, execute that candidate and then the standard π0.5 continuation, and output Y_k plus all r_{ij}; these rollback outcomes are training and evaluation labels only.
5. Train the permutation-equivariant quotient head on each full bundle, subtract its mean correction across candidates, and optimize pairwise center and interval losses; inputs are h_t, e_t, candidate actions, and WAM futures, and outputs are c_k and w_{ij}.
6. On held-out episodes, compute q_α from the maximum pair nonconformity per candidate bundle and choose α on the coverage-abstention frontier, producing one set-calibrated interval rule.
7. At deployment after each real prefix, generate K new executable candidate chunks, run the WAM and g_φ, compute e_t, and run one quotient-head forward pass to produce s_k and D_{ij}; no rollback or hidden simulator state enters this path.
8. Compute M_t and either execute the robust winner or invoke the L_safe fallback; this comparison changes which current π0.5 chunk reaches the robot, and the next real observation closes the receding-horizon loop.
9. Evaluate uncorrected WAM ranking, shared-gain residual injection, independent marginal residual regression, FBFM, and Residual Quotient on identical snapshots; output latent error, pairwise inversion rate, Kendall rank correlation, top-1 regret, task success, abstention rate, and inference latency.
10. Run the e_t permutation, branch-label shuffling, width ablation, and full rollback-oracle controls; each intervention propagates through D_{ij} and M_t to the selected physical action and final task success. Input guards require K>=2, remove any proprioceptive coordinate whose training-set sigma_p is zero before forming e_t, invoke the L_safe fallback if fewer than two candidates are returned, and resolve exact uncorrected fallback ties by the lowest sampler index.
final_candidate.falsification_prediction: Run open-weight π0.5 plus the DreamZero-compatible WAM on existing LIBERO and RoboTwin2.0 tasks with scripted mass, friction, occlusion, and contact perturbations; at each sampled current state evaluate K same-snapshot candidates and compare uncorrected ranking, shared-gain correction, independent marginal correction, FBFM, and Residual Quotient. If the mechanism works, pairwise inversion rate and top-1 regret decrease, Kendall rank correlation and task success increase, and the risk-abstention curve improves even in the subset where latent prediction error decreases under a naive correction. The named load-bearing variable is M_t, the minimum lower pairwise advantage of the best current candidate; permuting e_t across episodes or shuffling candidate labels before constructing r_{ij} should worsen downstream top-1 regret and task success toward the uncorrected baseline, not merely change M_t. A full rollback-oracle chooser supplies the upper bound, while a center-only head with w_{ij}=0 is the negative coverage control and should fail disproportionately under contact-mode changes.
